lastVerifiedRecord.description: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation of the Republic of Bulgaria hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals, which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Bulgarian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types: Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 500,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all other activities). Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.Type E: Phase 0/A/B1 small sat mission definition studies with potential to lead to either a national or a commercial mission, in the area of Earth Observation for Climate, Agriculture, Disaster Management and Environmental Monitoring, enabling the development and demonstration of Bulgarian technologies and products in space. Maximum price for ESA 300.000 Euros. Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 6 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000. To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.

record.description: The European Space Agency and the Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation of the Republic of Bulgaria hereby invite you to submit a proposal for the above Call for Proposals, which will be soon published in esa-star. While it is made visible to all ESA Member States, Associate Members and European Cooperating States, this CfP will be addressed only to Bulgarian legal entities registered in ESA-STAR, as prime tenderer and foresees the following standard activity types: Type A Research and Preparatory Activities, aimed at the preparation for participation in ESA optional programmes or the initial steps of a product development for Space, with potential for use on future ESA missions or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 1 and the target TRL shall be TRL3 or below. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. Type B Flight- and Ground Segment-related Research and Development Activities, targetting equipment to build competences and capabilities centred on products or generic technology development with potential for re-use on ESA or commercial missions. The start TRL shall be at least 3 and the target TRL shall be TRL 6. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 500,000 (hardware development)/EUR 250,000 (all other activities). Type D Space science activities, supporting the involvement of national researchers leading to potential of future involvement in ESA science mission core team and publication of peer reviewed scientific papers. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000.Type E: Phase 0/A/B1 small sat mission definition studies with potential to lead to either a national or a commercial mission, in the area of Earth Observation for Climate, Agriculture, Disaster Management and Environmental Monitoring, enabling the development and demonstration of Bulgarian technologies and products in space. Maximum price for ESA 300.000 Euros. Type F Space Applications, products and services making use of ESA/ European space infrastructure that is already existing or scheduled for operation in the near term. The start TRL shall be at least 6 and the target TRL shall be TRL 8. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 200,000. The work carried out by the Tenderer must be co-funded to a minimum level of 25% of the total cost of the activity. Type G1 University courses/modules leading to a qualification (BSc or MSc) in space related topics that correspond to the needs of national space industry and to encourage career in space and answer to national space industry needs. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 70,000. To be published as a separate tender in esa-star: Type G2 PhD Theses that correspond to a clear need from the national space industry and would lead to a new product or service being able to be developed. Maximum price for ESA: EUR 75,000 with a minimum company co-funding of EUR 10,000. More information and further programmatic constraints can be consulted in the cover letter of the call upon its issue date.

Details Unlocking Space for Business The UK Space Agency’s Unlocking Space for Business (USB) programme is seeking to accelerate the adoption of space-enabled data and services to address environmental intelligence and emissions challenges across the UK economy. This challenge-led competition is designed to support projects that demonstrate how space-enabled data, technologies and services can help organisations improve environmental monitoring, emissions measurement, reporting and verification, and wider environmental decision-making. The competition aims to stimulate greater collaboration between end users, data integrators and space-sector suppliers, while supporting the development of solutions with credible pathways to future operational adoption. Who can apply This competition is open to UK-registered end-user businesses, including SMEs, leading a consortium with at least one UK space supplier and any additional integrator or delivery partner organisations required to support project delivery. For the purposes of this competition, end-user businesses are organisations that use space-enabled products, services or insights to address operational challenges, improve decision-making, manage risk or deliver commercial outcomes. The competition is particularly aimed at end-user organisations operating in sectors including financial services, insurance, asset management, energy, utilities, infrastructure, agriculture, land management and environmental services. Applications from organisations in other sectors are also welcome, provided they can demonstrate a clear environmental intelligence or emissions-related use case aligned with the competition objectives. The UK Space Agency invites applications from end-user-led consortia comprising: An end-user organisation seeking to address one of the competition’s environmental intelligence or emissions challenge statements At least one supplier of space-enabled data, products or services; and Any additional delivery partners or integrators required to support successful project delivery. Applicant webinar The UK Space Agency will host an applicant webinar on 3 November 2026, 11:00 GMT to provide an overview of the competition, explain the challenge statements, outline the application process and answer participant questions. Interested organisations are strongly encouraged to attend. Details of how to register can be found Unlocking Space for Business: Environmental Intelligence and Emissions Grant Call Briefing Webinar. Funding available The UK Space Agency intends to award up to £2 million through this competition. Applicants may request up to £400,000 grant funding per project. Total project costs may be higher where match funding is provided by consortium partners. In exceptional circumstances, the UK Space Agency reserves the right to adjust the total funding available, the number of projects funded, or the value of individual awards. Project duration Projects are expected to start in January 2027 and run for approximately 9 months. Projects must be sufficiently mature to demonstrate operational value within the funded period and deliver measurable outcomes by the end of the project. How to apply Applications must be submitted through the Flexigrant portal by 16:00 GMT on 11 December 2026. Applicants must complete all required sections of the online application form and upload the required supporting documentation through the Flexigrant platform which can be accessed here: Flexigrant . Applications submitted by email will not be accepted. Late applications will not be accepted. Your application must include: A completed application form; Annex A: Proposed Milestone Table Annex B: Project Cost Breakdown Annex C: National Security Questionnaire (where required) Any additional supporting documentation requested within the application process. Applicants should read the full competition guidance before submitting an application. Sign up for emails or print this page Get emails about this page Print this page

Download the Application Package below to apply to ESA BIC Andalusia Download the Application Package (.zip)Who Can ApplyEnsure your startup can join our incubation programme To be eligible for ESA BIC Andalusia, your startup or business idea must meet the following criteria: Space-Related InnovationYour business must have a solid connection to space-related technology, expertise, or applications. This connection can be categorized as either Downstream or Upstream: Downstream This involves the application or exploitation of space systems or technologies in non-space domains. Your business idea may focus on: Applications utilizing satellite navigation, earth observation, or satellite communication.Technology transfer involving space-related hardware, software, or intellectual property.Providing solutions that leverage space data or technology to innovate in other sectorsUpstream This relates to the development of new technologies intended for use within the space sector. Examples include: Developing new systems, subsystems, or components for space missions.Technologies and services designed for use on space missions or in human spaceflight activities.Your application must clearly justify the space connection, demonstrating how it advances or innovates within the space sector. It is crucial that the space connection is clear and justified in your application. For further guidance on ensuring your idea meets the necessary criteria, please consult the Space Connection Assessment document. This will help you evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea to meet the requirements set by ESA BIC Andalusia. record.description: ApplyESA BIC Andalusia2026-10-29T15:23:31+01:00 Who Can ApplyEnsure your startup can join our incubation programme To be eligible for ESA BIC Andalusia, your startup or business idea must meet the following criteria: Space-Related InnovationYour business must have a solid connection to space-related technology, expertise, or applications. This connection can be categorized as either Downstream or Upstream: Downstream This involves the application or exploitation of space systems or technologies in non-space domains. Your business idea may focus on: Applications utilizing satellite navigation, earth observation, or satellite communication.Technology transfer involving space-related hardware, software, or intellectual property.Providing solutions that leverage space data or technology to innovate in other sectorsUpstream This relates to the development of new technologies intended for use within the space sector. Examples include: Developing new systems, subsystems, or components for space missions.Technologies and services designed for use on space missions or in human spaceflight activities.Your application must clearly justify the space connection, demonstrating how it advances or innovates within the space sector. It is crucial that the space connection is clear and justified in your application. For further guidance on ensuring your idea meets the necessary criteria, please consult the Space Connection Assessment document. This will help you evaluate and articulate the space connection of your business idea to meet the requirements set by ESA BIC Andalusia. Viable Business PlanYou must present a clear and viable business plan outlining your strategy for growth, the market potential of your product or service, and how your space-related innovation will be commercialized. The business plan should also detail financial projections, key milestones, and risk management strategies. Company AgeNew or existing companies less than 5 years old. If Your Company is Already Established Your startup must be legally registered in Spain and must not be older than five years at the time of application. If Your Company is Not Yet Established You are eligible to apply as an informal group of entrepreneurs, provided you commit to legally registering your startup in Andalusia upon acceptance into the programme. Company LocationYour business must be, or commit to being, located in Andalusia during the incubation period. ESA BIC Andalusia is strategically located in the Naves de Renfe building in the San Jerónimo district of Seville, near the Spanish Space Agency headquarters. Commitment to the programmeYour team must be fully committed to engaging with the ESA BIC Andalusia programme throughout the entire incubation period. This includes regular attendance at workshops, mentoring sessions, and events organized by the incubator, as well as making full use of the resources provided.
